# macOS OpenGL Performance Profiling Report — z1engine (Hybrid)

| | |
|---|---|
| Date | 2026-09-17 (evening session, ~23:00–23:50 CST) |
| Build | `Hybrid` (optimized + `DEBUG`/asserts), `python3 dev/z1.py compile --config Hybrid` |
| Scene | `content/helmet.yaml` — DamagedHelmet + grid plane, deferred pipeline, TAA + GTAO + bloom + 4-cascade CSM all enabled |
| Method | temporary `[TEMP-PROBE]` frame instrumentation (wall-clock scopes + optional GL knobs), on-screen verification with `screencapture` |

---

## 1. TL;DR

1. **The app is not CPU-bound.** All CPU-side work together is **~1.2–1.7 ms/frame** regardless of resolution
   (scene update 0.01 ms, renderer CPU submit ~1.1 ms, ImGui ~0.47 ms, event poll ~0.11 ms).
2. **Rendering cost scales with the render resolution, not with scene complexity.** The helmet scene renders
   30 draw calls; the GPU time is dominated by full-screen passes. Per-megapixel cost rises superlinearly:

   | Editor viewport | megapixels | steady fps | frame time | ms / Mpx |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | 640×480 (default) | 0.31 | ~80–88 | ~12 ms | ~13 |
   | 800×600 | 0.48 | 53.9 | 18.6 ms | ~21 |
   | 1280×720 | 0.92 | 29.0 | 34.5 ms | ~29 |
   | 1920×1080 | 2.07 | 11.9 | 84 ms | ~37 |
   | 2560×1440 | 3.69 | 5.4 | 185 ms | ~48 |

3. **A fixed macOS present-path cost of ~8–9 ms/frame exists even with rendering skipped** (120 fps ceiling).
   This is the `glfwSwapBuffers` page-flip/compositor floor on this machine, not a bug in the engine.
4. **Game mode** renders the scene at the window's 1× drawable (1280×720) and runs at **~33–36 fps** — several
   full-screen effects at once are simply beyond an Intel Iris Plus 645 without quality knobs.
5. **GTAO is the single most expensive pass** at high resolution: disabling it recovers **~32–36 ms at 1080p**
   (13 → 22.5 fps cold; 11.5 → 19.6 fps in a warmer interleaved re-run). TAA+velocity ~13–16 ms, bloom
   ~2–4 ms, CSM shadows ~0–2.5 ms (resolution-dependent).
6. Two real macOS quirks were found (display-sleep abort; GL timer-query availability) plus one vsync
   bookkeeping bug (`WindowData::v_sync` says ON, GLFW swap interval is actually 0). No swapchain or window
   size bug was found.

**What "very slow" corresponds to in practice:**
- Editor with the viewport resolution set to ≥1080p (13 fps; verified on screen: FPS 13.6 / Frame 73.68 ms), or
- Game mode at its default 1280×720 (35 fps), degrading with window size (a maximized game window is worse), or
- The first ~1–2 s after launch (single-frame stalls of 0.9–1.3 s from shader/pipeline compilation).

## 3. Method & instrumentation

The measurements were taken with a temporary probe (call sites marked `[TEMP-PROBE]`). That probe has since
been **formalized** into `engine/runtime/source/util/prober.{h,cpp}`, compiled in with `ENABLE_PROBING` —
an **opt-in** define for the `Hybrid` configuration, enabled by generating the projects with
`./generate.sh --probing` (or `python dev/z1.py generate --probing`); see §8. The scope layout stayed the
same:

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `util/prober.{h,cpp}` (new) | wall-clock frame/scope accumulator + GPU timer queries; prints a `[probe]` report every 120 frames + final summary |
| `core/application.cpp` | loop scopes `update` / `imgui` / `window_update` / `swap`, `draws` counter |
| `editor_layer.cpp` | scopes `scene_update` / `renderer_draw` / `picking` |
| `imgui_layer.cpp` | scopes `imgui_begin` / `imgui_drawdata` / `imgui_platform` / `imgui_end` |
| `core/window.cpp` | `glfw_poll` scope |
| `render/rhi/opengl_context.{h,cpp}` | `glfw_swap` timing; GL_TIME_ELAPSED query ring |

During the investigation additional **temporary** pass knobs were used for A/B tests (`Z1_PROBE_SKIP_RENDER`,
`NO_AO`, `AO_QUARTER`, `NO_TAA`, `NO_BLOOM`, `NO_SHADOWS`, `SHADOW_RES`, `GAME_CAMERA`). They no longer exist;
the equivalent experiments are now configuration-driven (`sm_resolution`, `sm_cascade_count`, `ao_resolution`,
`taa_enabled`, `pp_bloom_enabled`, `ssr_enabled`, or a quality preset — see §8).

**Environment variables of the probing build**

```
Z1_PROBE_EVERY=N        report interval in frames (default 120, 0 disables reports)
Z1_PROBE_QUIET=1        suppress periodic reports (environment line + final summary stay)
Z1_PROBE_VSYNC=0|1      force swap interval at startup
Z1_PROBE_FINISH=1       glFinish() before swap (drain probe, reported as gpu_drain)
Z1_PROBE_NO_GPU=1       disable GPU timer queries
Z1_NO_GL_CHECK=1        disable glGetError() polling
```

**Caveats / measurement notes**

- All measurements are frame wall time in steady state (startup window excluded unless stated). Primary
  metric is the frame-time delta between configurations measured back-to-back in one session.
- The machine shows **±5–15 % run-to-run variance** from thermal drift during long sweeps (e.g. the same
  640×480 configuration measured 87.8 fps early and ~78–84 fps later in the evening). Pass deltas that are
  < 3 ms should be considered noise at 1080p.
- `GL_TIME_ELAPSED` samples are **unreliable on this driver**: `GL_QUERY_RESULT_AVAILABLE` stays false unless
  the command stream syncs (e.g. a `glFinish`); with `Z1_PROBE_FINISH=1` samples flow (298/359 frames), but
  `glFinish` itself serialises the pipeline. GPU attribution in this report therefore comes from
  *pass-toggle deltas*, not from timer queries. Values when they were available: ImGui+picking GPU ≈ 0.45 ms.
- The app was kept awake with `caffeinate -dims`; with the display asleep the editor **aborts** (see §5.2).
- Launch runs with `--frames=N` for the editor. The game mode currently ignores `--frames`
  (it runs until killed) — use `perl -e 'alarm(60); exec @ARGV'` to bound it.
- Probe overhead is small and included in all numbers (a few chrono calls + 2 GL calls/frame). Disabling the
  GL query ring (`Z1_PROBE_NO_GPU=1`) changed editor timings by less than the run-to-run variance.

## 4. Results

### 4.1 Editor steady state @640×480 (default viewport) — long run, 3600 frames

| scope | avg (whole run) | steady windows | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| frame | 13.01 ms | **~12.3 ms** | max 1273 ms (startup only) |
| swap (incl. `glfwSwapBuffers`) | 10.70 ms | ~10.4 ms | the present floor |
| update (layers) | 1.65 ms | ~1.1 ms | scene_update 0.008 + renderer_draw ~1.09 + picking 0.06 |
| imgui (all) | 0.47 ms | ~0.47 ms | begin 0.09 + drawdata 0.12 + end 0.12 |
| window_update (poll) | 0.11 ms | ~0.10 ms | |
| draws | 30 | 30 | |

Steady fps ≈ **78–88** depending on how warm the machine is. Even here, **~85 % of the frame is spent
waiting in `glfwSwapBuffers`.**

The on-screen editor stats panel matches the probe (verified at 1080p via screenshot: *FPS 13.6, Frame Time
73.68 ms* — probe measured 73–84 ms in that configuration).

### 4.2 Viewport resolution sweep (editor, same scene)

| viewport | steady fps | frame | swap | derived scene cost | ms/Mpx |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 640×480 | ~80 (12.3 ms steady) | 12.3 ms | 10.4 ms | ~4.0 ms | ~13 |
| 800×600 | 53.9 | 18.6 ms | ~15.8 ms | ~10.3 ms | ~21 |
| 1280×720 | 29.0 | 34.5 ms | ~30.2 ms | ~26.2 ms | ~29 |
| 1920×1080 | 11.9 | 84 ms | ~70 ms | ~76 ms | ~37 |
| 2560×1440 | 5.4 | 185 ms | ~173 ms | ~177 ms | ~48 |

The cost per pixel roughly **doubles between 480p and 1440p**, i.e. the pipeline (5-attachment float
G-buffer, RGBA32F TAA history, full-res bloom chain, GTAO, CSM) is bandwidth/driver-limited on this iGPU.

### 4.3 Pass isolation @1920×1080 viewport (interleaved runs, 240 frames each)

| config | steady fps | frame | delta vs baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| baseline #1 | 13.1 | 76.3 ms | – |
| `NO_AO` | 22.5 | 44.4 ms | **−31.9 ms (GTAO)** |
| `NO_TAA` (incl. velocity) | 15.9 | 62.9 ms | **−13.4 ms (TAA + velocity)** |
| `NO_BLOOM` | 13.4 | 74.6 ms | −1.7 ms (≈ noise) |
| `NO_SHADOWS` | 12.1 | 82.6 ms | ≈ 0 (within drift) |
| baseline #2 | 12.3 | 81.3 ms | – |
| all four off | 47.8 | 20.9 ms | **−57 ms** |

At 640×480 the same toggles are cheap (all-effects-off 120 fps vs 87.8 fps baseline ⇒ whole stack ~2.5 ms),
but **CSM shadows dominate there**: `SHADOW_RES=512` recovered ~2.5 ms (8.9 ms frame, 112.8 fps).

**AO cost at 1080p (interleaved 600-frame runs, same session):** baseline 11.5–11.6 fps (86–87 ms),
`NO_AO` 19.6 fps (51.0 ms) ⇒ **GTAO ≈ 35 ms** (consistent with the ~32 ms measured earlier, colder, in the
interleaved matrix above).

**AO resolution experiment (`Z1_PROBE_AO_QUARTER`, half → quarter res @1080p):** in the cleanest
back-to-back pair the frame went **75.2 ms → 57.1 ms (13.3 → 17.5 fps), recovering ~18 ms** with AO still
enabled. Three bracketed repeats measured −20.5 / −9.8 / −21.4 ms (mean ≈ **17 ms**, ≈ half of the GTAO
cost; the remainder behaves like pass-structure / fetch-latency cost rather than per-pixel work). For
reference, fully disabling AO in the same session recovered ~29–42 ms (spread reflects thermal drift).
At 640×480 the same change is ~1 ms (87.1 → 97.3 fps), consistent with AO being cheap at low resolution.

### 4.4 Game mode (deferred stack at full window resolution)

| run | steady | frame | swap | CPU update | draws |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--game --scene=helmet` @1280×720 (1× drawable) | 33–36 fps | 28–30 ms | 27–28 ms | 1.2–1.3 ms | 28 |

(from two sessions: 60 s bounded run 32.7–36.7 fps; earlier 480-frame run 33–35 fps)

Game mode renders the *same* deferred stack but without the editor ImGui overlay, at the window's 1×
drawable. It is effectively always GPU/present-bound; increasing the window size scales cost by pixel count
(a maximized 1440×900 window ≈ 1.3 Mpx ⇒ ≈ 40 ms ≈ 25 fps; a 1920×1080 window ⇒ ≈ 15 fps).

Two ergonomics findings for the game path:
- `--frames=N` is not honoured by `GameApp`; only the editor exits on its own. Automation needs a wrapper.
- Editor-authored scenes keep their main camera transient, so `--game --scene=<editor scene>` fails with
  *"No main camera found"* unless a camera entity is authored explicitly (`Z1_PROBE_GAME_CAMERA=1` was used
  to profile the game path in the meantime).

### 4.5 The macOS present floor and pacing

| experiment | result | interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| renderer skipped, window 1280×720 | 120 fps, frame ~8.3 ms, GPU ≈ 0.45 ms | floor is not GPU work |
| renderer skipped, viewport 1920×1080 | 120 fps, frame 8.9 ms | floor is resolution-independent |
| window 640×360 / 1280×720 / 1379×847 | same frame time | floor is not backbuffer size |
| `VSYNC=1` | ~52–57 fps, swap 11.1 ms | vsync lock behaves normally (~60 Hz with occasional missed deadlines) |
| `FINISH=1` (glFinish before swap) | frame 21.6 ms, "gpu" 10.9 ms | glFinish serialises; not a pure GPU-busy metric |

The floor (~7.5–10 ms) is Apple's GL-over-Metal present path on this machine. Practically it means the app
can never exceed ~120 fps, and at 640×480 it spends ~85 % of each frame in the swap call even though only
~2.5–4 ms of real work exists.

### 4.6 Startup behaviour

- `app launch (ms)` ≈ **487–757 ms** across runs (asset scan, Python init, first pipelines).
- First ~1–2 s of rendering contain single-frame stalls of **0.9–1.3 s** (`renderer_draw` max 885–1040 ms) —
  shader/pipeline compilation and first-use driver work; the first 120-frame window reports 33–38 fps before
  settling.
- No comparable stalls occur afterwards for the helmet scene (steady-state max frame ≈ 20–25 ms).

### 4.7 Ruled out (measured, not guesses)

| Hypothesis | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| CPU bottleneck | No | total CPU 1.2–1.7 ms/frame at all resolutions; scene update 0.008 ms |
| `glGetError()` polling overhead | No | `Z1_NO_GL_CHECK=1` run: 90.0 fps — identical |
| ImGui cost (CPU or GPU) | No | 0.47 ms CPU; ~0.45 ms GPU (timer sample in skip-render mode) |
| Window/backbuffer size (UI fill) | No | frame time invariant across window sizes |
| Swapchain framebuffer size mismatch | No | `WindowData == glfwGetFramebufferSize == 1280×720` at runtime (1× surface) |
| Picking / scene update | No | picking 0.05 ms; scene update 0.008 ms |
| Vsync throttling by default | No | swap interval is 0 (GLFW default); vsync-off tearing instead |

## 5. Findings on macOS specifics

1. **Retina hint behaviour.** `GLFW_COCOA_RETINA_FRAMEBUFFER=FALSE` results in a **1× drawable at runtime**
   (verified: `win=WindowData=fb=1280×720`). Immediately after `glfwCreateWindow` the framebuffer *reads back*
   as 2560×1440 (before AppKit finalises the surface) — this was an early red herring; there is no persistent
   mismatch. Note the rendering is therefore soft on the Retina panel (1× upscaled by the compositor), which
   is the intended trade-off here.
2. **Display sleep aborts the editor** (Hybrid/Debug): with the display off, the ImGui multi-viewport backend
   asserts `Platform init didn't setup Monitors list?` (`imgui.cpp:9707`) and the process dies. Keep the
   display awake (`caffeinate -u`/`-d`) for automated runs; consider guarding this in code if it can happen
   during unattended use.
3. **`GL_TIME_ELAPSED` queries are unreliable on this driver** (`QUERY_RESULT_AVAILABLE` stays false unless
   the stream syncs); plan profiling around wall-clock deltas or force sync (costly).
4. **Vsync bookkeeping mismatch.** `WindowData::v_sync` defaults to `true` (checkbox renders as ON) but
   `glfwSwapInterval` is never called at startup, so the app actually runs vsync-**off**. Either call
   `set_v_sync(m_data.v_sync)` during init or default the flag to `false`.
5. (carried from earlier sessions) No KHR_debug on macOS: no `glDebugMessageCallback`, render-graph debug
   groups are no-ops; `glCheckError()` polling is the only localisation tool.

---

## 6. Recommendations (ranked by measured payoff)

1. **Give GTAO a quality/resolution knob — it is the top cost at high res (~32–36 ms @1080p).**
   Validated: quarter-resolution AO (`Z1_PROBE_AO_QUARTER`) recovers **~17 ms @1080p** (clean pair:
   75.2 → 57.1 ms, 13.3 → 17.5 fps) while keeping the effect. Remaining cost can be attacked with fewer
   slices/steps (currently 6 slices × 8 steps × 2 sides = 96 depth taps/px at half res) or a denoise pass
   instead of high sample counts.
2. **TAA + velocity ≈ 13–16 ms @1080p** — make TAA optional at high resolutions or cheapen the velocity pass.
3. **Add a render-scale (or resolution warning) for the editor viewport.** 1280×720 viewport is already only
   29 fps and 1080p is 12 fps on this machine; the default 640×480 is the only fluid option today.
4. **Reduce CSM shadow maps on iGPU** (2048² × 4 cascades ⇒ ~2.5 ms @640×480; 1024 should save ~1.5–2 ms,
   512 measured 2.5 ms total saving). At 1080p they are hidden under the bigger passes but not free.
5. **Default to vsync or a ~60 fps cap.** The app currently renders uncapped (100 % GPU busy, tearing,
   battery/heat on a thin laptop); there is ample headroom at 640×480 to hold 60 fps with vsync on.
6. **Soften the startup hitches** (0.9–1.3 s single frames during the first ~2 s): pre-warm/async-compile
   pipelines+shaders, or hide them behind a loading screen; users restarting the editor feel this every launch.
7. **Housekeeping fixes:** honour `--frames` in game mode (automation/smoke parity); fix the vsync flag
   bookkeeping; keep the display-awake guard for ImGui multi-viewport.

## 8. Follow-up: probing + quality settings (implemented)

The temporary instrumentation was formalized and the top recommendations were implemented in the change
`add-probing-and-quality-presets`:

- **Probing is a first-class, opt-in build feature** — `util/prober.{h,cpp}`, compiled in via
  `ENABLE_PROBING` when projects are generated with `--probing` (`Hybrid`), with `PROBE_SCOPE` /
  `PROBE_VALUE` / `PROBE_FRAME_BEGIN/END` macros and GPU timer queries; no-ops in every other
  configuration and in default (no-flag) builds (no runtime cost).
- **Quality presets (editor only)** — `LOW` / `MEDIUM` / `HIGH`, selected in the global settings panel and
  persisted in `editor_settings.yaml`. `LOW` turns TAA (+sharpen), bloom and SSR off, drops AO to quarter
  resolution and shadows to 1024² × 1 cascade; `MEDIUM` = 2048² × 2 cascades with TAA (no sharpen);
  `HIGH` = 2048² × 4 cascades, TAA + sharpen, half-res AO (the previous defaults). Game builds configure
  the same settings from script instead of using presets.
- **Configurable shadows** — `sm_resolution` (512/1024/2048/4096) and `sm_cascade_count` (1–4) are global
  settings; the renderer allocates exactly that many cascades and the shaders never sample missing layers.
- **Configurable AO resolution** — `ao_resolution` (half/quarter).
- **Render-graph pass skipping** — with `taa_enabled` off the velocity/TAA/sharpen passes are not added at all
  (post-process reads the scene color directly); with `pp_bloom_enabled` off the whole bloom chain is skipped.
- **macOS fixes** — the advertised vsync state is applied to the context at startup
  (`glfwSwapInterval`), and the render loop skips UI/ImGui work while no display is attached (display
  asleep) instead of aborting on ImGui's monitor-list assert.
